Hadid
HAY-did
proper noun
Hebrew chadid, “sharp” or “pointed,” a town of Benjamin reinhabited by the children of the captivity after the return from Babylon.

📖 Biblical Definition

Hadid was a town in the territory of Benjamin, lying toward the western lowland, that is named among the places reinhabited by the children of the captivity when they came up out of Babylon. In the great register of those who returned with Zerubbabel, the men of Lod, Hadid, and Ono are numbered together (Ezr 2:33), and the same households appear again in the parallel record of Nehemiah (Neh 7:37), and once more among the villages where the men of Benjamin dwelt after the wall was built (Neh 11:34). So Hadid is a town of the restoration, a place repeopled by the mercy of God after the long desolation of the exile. The dictionary records Hadid that the reader may behold the faithfulness of the LORD, who did not cast off His people for ever, but brought a remnant home to the old inheritance and set them again in their cities. The lines that had fallen to Benjamin in pleasant places were possessed afresh, the ancient landmarks were owned again, and Hadid was numbered once more among the dwellings of the covenant people. It bears witness that the God who scatters in judgment gathers in mercy, and keeps the bounds of His people’s habitation even through captivity and return.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A town of Benjamin toward the lowland, reinhabited by the returned exiles after the captivity in Babylon.

expand to see more

HADID, a town of Benjamin, lying toward the western lowland near Lod and Ono.

It is named among the places reinhabited by the children of the captivity who returned from Babylon.

The men of Lod, Hadid, and Ono are numbered together in the registers of Ezra and Nehemiah.

It appears among the villages where the men of Benjamin dwelt after the wall was built.

It witnesses to the LORD’s faithfulness in bringing a remnant home to the old inheritance.

📖 Key Scripture

Ezr 2:33 — "The children of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred twenty and five."

Pro 22:28 — "Remove not the ancient landmark, which thy fathers have set."

Psa 16:6 — "The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage."

Act 17:26 — "And hath made of one blood all nations of men for to dwell on all the face of the earth, and hath determined the times before appointed, and the bounds of their habitation;"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; it witnesses to the LORD’s sovereign apportioning of every saint’s portion.

expand to see more

Hadid is a town of the sacred geography, and no movement of the present age has troubled itself to redefine it. The dictionary records it that the reader who meets the name among the returned exiles may know it for a real place in a real inheritance, repeopled by a real God who kept faith with a real people through their captivity.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the faithfulness of God to His covenant remnant. He who brought the men of Hadid home from Babylon to their old town is the same who has determined the times before appointed and the bounds of every habitation. The saint who has known scattering and loss may remember Hadid, and trust the God who gathers in mercy what He has scattered in judgment, and keeps the bounds of His people through every exile.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew for “sharp,” Hadid names a town of Benjamin repeopled after the exile.

expand to see more

Hadid — Hebrew chadid, “sharp” or “pointed.”

It lay in the territory of Benjamin toward the western lowland.

It is named with Lod and Ono among the returned exiles.

Its men appear in the registers of both Ezra and Nehemiah.

It was reinhabited after the captivity in Babylon.

Usage

"Like Hadid repeopled after the exile, the LORD restores His people to the heritage He gave their fathers."

"The God who gathers a remnant home keeps the ancient landmark for those who return to Him."

"A town reinhabited after captivity reminds us that mercy follows judgment for the covenant people."
